# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

### Create IFC Beam with Geometry Representation

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

This snippet shows how to create an IfcBeam entity, define its placement, assign it a type, and create a geometric representation using a predefined profile. It utilizes IFCopenShell's API for entity creation and geometry handling.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.api
import ifcopenshell.util.representation
from ifcopenshell import geom

# Assume 'model', 'beam_type', and 'hea100' are pre-defined IFC objects/values
# Example: model = ifcopenshell.file.create()
# Example: beam_type = ifcopenshell.api.type.add_type(model, 'B1BeamType', 'IfcBeam')
# Example: hea100 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_profile(model, 'HEA100', 'IPE')

# Create an IfcBeam entity
beam = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcBeam")

# Edit the object placement for the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=beam)

# Assign the beam type to the created beam
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[beam], relating_type=beam_type)

# Get the 'Body' model context
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")

# Create a profile representation for the beam's geometry
representation = geom.add_profile_representation(model, context=body, profile=hea100, depth=1)

# Assign the created geometry representation back to the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=beam, representation=representation)
```

### Process IFC Element to Shape Data (Python)

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_processing.rst

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

    # A more human readable name
    print(style.name)

    # Each style may have diffuse colour RGB codes
    if style.has_diffuse:
        print(style.diffuse)

    # Each style may have transparency data
    if style.has_transparency:
        print(style.transparency)

# Indices of material applied per triangle face e.g. [f1m, f2m, ...]
material_ids = shape.geometry.material_ids

# IDs representation item per triangle face e.g. [f1i, f2i, ...]
item_ids = shape.geometry.item_ids

### Manually Create Extruded Rectangle Representation - Python

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

Illustrates how to manually create an IFC shape representation for an extruded rectangle without using the shape builder utility. This involves defining a rectangle profile and an extrusion solid, then combining them into an IFC shape representation. This method requires a deeper understanding of IFC geometry concepts.

```python
rectangle = model.createIfcRectangleProfileDef(ProfileType="AREA", XDim=500, YDim=250)
direction = model.createIfcDirection((0., 0., 1.))
extrusion = model.createIfcExtrudedAreaSolid(SweptArea=rectangle, ExtrudedDirection=direction, Depth=1000)
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")
representation = model.createIfcShapeRepresentation(
    ContextOfItems=body, RepresentationIdentifier="Body", RepresentationType="SweptSolid", Items=[extrusion])
```

import ifcopenshell.api
import ifcopenshell.util.representation

# Assume 'model', 'beam_type', and 'hea100' are pre-defined IFC objects/values

# Example: hea100 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_profile(model, 'HEA100', 'IPE')

# Create an IfcBeam entity
beam = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcBeam")

# Edit the object placement for the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=beam)

# Assign the beam type to the created beam
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[beam], relating_type=beam_type)

# Get the 'Body' model context
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")

# Create a profile representation for the beam's geometry

        else:
            print(f"Space {space.Name}: No section created")
            
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error processing space {space.Name}: {e}")

verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
print(f"Vertices: {verts.shape}")

unique_points, indices = np.unique(xy_points_rounded, axis=0, return_index=True)
print(f"Unique XY points: {len(unique_points)}")

hull_points = unique_points[hull.vertices]
print(f"Hull points: {hull_points}")

print(f"Hull polygon valid: {hull_polygon.is_valid}")
print(f"Hull polygon area: {hull_polygon.area}")

    print("PASS: Bounding box fits (rotated)")
else:
    print("FAIL: Bounding box too small")

print(f"Rotated rect dimensions: X={rect_dim_x:.2f}, Y={rect_dim_y:.2f}")

if rect_dim_x >= req_width and rect_dim_y >= req_depth:

    print("PASS: Min rotated rectangle fits (rotated)")

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

# Indices of material applied per triangle face e.g. [f1m, f2m, ...]

# IDs representation item per triangle face e.g. [f1i, f2i, ...]

The algorithm will: 1) Load IFC model and classify spaces, 2) Extract 2D footprint geometry using trimesh sections, 3) Check if a 760mm x 1220mm rectangle can fit using shapely. The check tries multiple orientations (0, 90, 45, 30, 60 degrees) and samples placement locations at centroid, vertices, and random interior points.
answer.python_code:
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import trimesh
import shapely.geometry as geom
import shapely.ops as ops
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Optional
import warnings

# Suppress trimesh warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')

def get_space_footprint(space, model) -> Optional[geom.Polygon]:
    """Extract 2D footprint from an IfcSpace."""
    try:
        settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
        settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
        
        shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
        verts = shape.geometry.verts
        faces = shape.geometry.faces
        
        verts_array = np.array(verts).reshape(-1, 3)
        mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts_array, faces=faces)
        
        bounds = mesh.bounds
        z_min, z_max = bounds[0, 2], bounds[1, 2]
        z_mid = (z_min + z_max) / 2
        
        section = mesh.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, z_mid], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
        if section is None:
            return None
            
        path2d = section.to_planar()[0]
        if not path2d.polygons_full:
            return None
            
        return path2d.polygons_full[0]
    except Exception:
        return None

def can_fit_rectangle(polygon: geom.Polygon, width: float, depth: float) -> bool:
    """Check if a rectangle of given dimensions can fit inside the polygon."""
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = polygon.bounds
    poly_width = maxx - minx
    poly_depth = maxy - miny
    
    if poly_width < width or poly_depth < depth:
        if poly_width >= depth and poly_depth >= width:
            pass
        else:
            return False
    
    if not polygon.is_valid:
        polygon = polygon.buffer(0)
        if polygon.is_empty or not polygon.is_valid:
            return False
    
    orientations = [0, 90, 45, 30, 60]
    
    for angle_deg in orientations:
        angle_rad = np.radians(angle_deg)
        cos_a, sin_a = np.cos(angle_rad), np.sin(angle_rad)
        
        centroid = polygon.centroid
        candidate_centers = [centroid]
        
        if isinstance(polygon, geom.Polygon):
            coords = list(polygon.exterior.coords)
            for pt in coords:
                point = geom.Point(pt)
                if polygon.contains(point.buffer(1)):
                    candidate_centers.append(point)
        
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = polygon.bounds
        for _ in range(15):
            x = np.random.uniform(minx, maxx)
            y = np.random.uniform(miny, maxy)
            pt = geom.Point(x, y)
            if polygon.contains(pt):
                candidate_centers.append(pt)
        
        for center in candidate_centers:
            cx, cy = center.x, center.y
            corners_local = [
                (-width/2, -depth/2),
                (width/2, -depth/2),
                (width/2, depth/2),
                (-width/2, depth/2)
            ]
            
            corners_rotated = []
            for x, y in corners_local:
                xr = x * cos_a - y * sin_a
                yr = x * sin_a + y * cos_a
                corners_rotated.append((cx + xr, cy + yr))
            
            rect = geom.Polygon(corners_rotated)
            if rect.is_valid and polygon.contains(rect):
                return True
    
    return False

def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Check if spaces have accessible clear floor space per rule 305.3.
    
    Rule: 305.3 Size
    The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) minimum 
    by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate the rule (spaces that
        cannot accommodate a 760mm x 1220mm clear floor area).
    """
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    space_dicts = [{'guid': s.GlobalId, 'name': s.LongName or s.Name or ''} for s in spaces]
    classified_spaces = classify_spaces(space_dicts, path_ifc_model)
    
    applicable_classifications = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional',
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production',
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    violating_guids = []
    min_width = 760  # mm
    min_depth = 1220  # mm
    
    for i, space in enumerate(spaces):
        classification = classified_spaces[i].get('classification', 'Unclassified')
        
        if classification not in applicable_classifications:
            continue
        
        footprint = get_space_footprint(space, model)
        if footprint is None:
            continue
        
        if not can_fit_rectangle(footprint, min_width, min_depth):
            violating_guids.append(space.GlobalId)
    
    return violating_guids

### Create IFC Beam with Geometry Representation

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

This snippet shows how to create an IfcBeam entity, define its placement, assign it a type, and create a geometric representation using a predefined profile. It utilizes IFCopenShell's API for entity creation and geometry handling.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.api
import ifcopenshell.util.representation
from ifcopenshell import geom

# Assume 'model', 'beam_type', and 'hea100' are pre-defined IFC objects/values
# Example: model = ifcopenshell.file.create()
# Example: beam_type = ifcopenshell.api.type.add_type(model, 'B1BeamType', 'IfcBeam')
# Example: hea100 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_profile(model, 'HEA100', 'IPE')

# Create an IfcBeam entity
beam = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcBeam")

# Edit the object placement for the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=beam)

# Assign the beam type to the created beam
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[beam], relating_type=beam_type)

# Get the 'Body' model context
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")

# Create a profile representation for the beam's geometry
representation = geom.add_profile_representation(model, context=body, profile=hea100, depth=1)

# Assign the created geometry representation back to the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=beam, representation=representation)
```

### Process IFC Element to Shape Data (Python)

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_processing.rst

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

    # A more human readable name
    print(style.name)

    # Each style may have diffuse colour RGB codes
    if style.has_diffuse:
        print(style.diffuse)

    # Each style may have transparency data
    if style.has_transparency:
        print(style.transparency)

# Indices of material applied per triangle face e.g. [f1m, f2m, ...]
material_ids = shape.geometry.material_ids

# IDs representation item per triangle face e.g. [f1i, f2i, ...]
item_ids = shape.geometry.item_ids

import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape
import shapely.geometry as sg
import shapely.ops as so
import numpy as np
import trimesh
from typing import List

# Define the helper function
def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Check ADA 305.3 Size compliance for spaces in an IFC model.
    
    Rule 305.3: The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) minimum 
    by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Applicable Space Classifications: Balcony, Circulation, Garage, Habitable, 
    Institutional, Lobby, Mercantile, Office, Parking, Production, Refuge, 
    Stair Hall, Workplace
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List[str]: List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate the rule (have 
                   inaccessible areas where a 760mm x 1220mm clear space cannot fit).
                   Returns empty list if no violations or if model cannot be processed.
                   
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('/path/to/model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violating spaces")
    """
    # Constants for minimum clear space (mm)
    MIN_WIDTH = 760.0  # 30 inches
    MIN_LENGTH = 1220.0  # 48 inches
    
    # Applicable classifications
    APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional',
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production',
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped = 0
    
    try:
        model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Could not open IFC model: {e}")
        return []
    
    # Get all spaces
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Prepare space data for classification
    space_data = []
    for space in spaces:
        space_info = {
            'guid': space.GlobalId,
            'name': space.LongName or space.Name or "",
            'obj': space
        }
        space_data.append(space_info)
    
    # Classify spaces
    try:
        classified_spaces = classify_spaces(space_data, path_ifc_model)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Could not classify spaces: {e}")
        # Proceed without classification - check all spaces
        classified_spaces = space_data
    
    # Process each space
    settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
    
    for space_info in classified_spaces:
        space = space_info.get('obj')
        classification = space_info.get('classification', 'Unclassified')
        
        if space is None:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        
        # Skip spaces not in applicable classifications
        if classification not in APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS:
            continue
        
        try:
            # Get geometry for the space
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
            faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)
            
            # Create trimesh
            mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts, faces=faces)
            
            # Get z-level for section (mid-height of space)
            min_z, max_z = mesh.bounds[0, 2], mesh.bounds[1, 2]
            mid_z = (min_z + max_z) / 2
            
            # Create horizontal section to get 2D footprint
            section = mesh.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, mid_z], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
            
            if section:
                path2d = section.to_planar()[0]
                if path2d.polygons_full:
                    polygon = path2d.polygons_full[0]
                    
                    # Check if the space can fit the minimum rectangle
                    # Use minimum rotated rectangle to find tightest bounding box
                    min_rect = polygon.minimum_rotated_rectangle
                    
                    if isinstance(min_rect, sg.Polygon):
                        # Get the dimensions of the minimum rotated rectangle
                        coords = list(min_rect.exterior.coords)
                        # Calculate edge lengths
                        edge1_len = sg.Point(coords[0]).distance(sg.Point(coords[1]))
                        edge2_len = sg.Point(coords[1]).distance(sg.Point(coords[2]))
                        
                        # The rectangle dimensions are the two perpendicular edge lengths
                        width = min(edge1_len, edge2_len)
                        length = max(edge1_len, edge2_len)
                        
                        # Convert to mm (IFC models are typically in mm, but check bounds)
                        # If bounds suggest meters (large numbers), convert
                        max_extent = max(mesh.extents)
                        if max_extent > 1000:  # Likely in millimeters already
                            scale_factor = 1.0
                        else:  # Likely in meters
                            scale_factor = 1000.0
                        
                        width_mm = width * scale_factor
                        length_mm = length * scale_factor
                        
                        # Check violation: space is too small in either dimension
                        if width_mm < MIN_WIDTH or length_mm < MIN_LENGTH:
                            violating_guids.append(space.GlobalId)
            else:
                # No section could be created - space may have degenerate geometry
                # Consider this a violation as it indicates inaccessible area
                violating_guids.append(space.GlobalId)
                
        except Exception as e:
            # If geometry processing fails, consider it a potential violation
            # (inaccessible area due to geometry issues)
            skipped += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped} spaces due to geometry processing errors")
    
    return violating_guids

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_processing.rst

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

    # A more human readable name
    print(style.name)

    # Each style may have diffuse colour RGB codes
    if style.has_diffuse:
        print(style.diffuse)

    # Each style may have transparency data
    if style.has_transparency:
        print(style.transparency)

# Indices of material applied per triangle face e.g. [f1m, f2m, ...]
material_ids = shape.geometry.material_ids

# IDs representation item per triangle face e.g. [f1i, f2i, ...]
item_ids = shape.geometry.item_ids

This Python code snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an element, and create its OpenCASCADE BRep geometry. It utilizes ifcopenshell.geom.settings to enable Python-OCC and retrieves the transformation and translation part of the shape.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
settings.set("use-python-opencascade", True)

try:
    shape = geom.create_shape(settings, element)
    geometry = shape.geometry # see #1124
    # These are methods of the TopoDS_Shape class from pythonOCC
    shape_gpXYZ = geometry.Location().Transformation().TranslationPart()
    # These are methods of the gpXYZ class from pythonOCC
    print(shape_gpXYZ.X(), shape_gpXYZ.Y(), shape_gpXYZ.Z())
except:
    print("Shape creation failed")

### Get XYZ Coordinates of an IFC Element with IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/code_examples.rst

This example shows how to extract the XYZ coordinates (location) of an IFC element from its placement information. It uses `ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement` to obtain the transformation matrix and then extracts the translation vector. Assumes an IFC model is loaded and an 'IfcWall' instance is available.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.placement

model = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')

wall = model.by_type("IfcWall")[0]
# This returns a 4x4 matrix, including the location and rotation. For example:
# array([[ 1.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00, 2.00000000e+00],
#        [ 0.00000000e+00,  1.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00, 3.00000000e+00],
#        [ 0.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00,  1.00000000e+00, 5.00000000e+00],
#        [ 0.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00, 1.00000000e+00]])
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
# The last column holds the XYZ values, such as:
# array([ 2.00000000e+00,  3.00000000e+00,  5.00000000e+00])
print(matrix[:,3][:3])

def get_space_footprint(space, model) -> Optional[geom.Polygon]:
    """Extract 2D footprint from an IfcSpace."""
    try:
        settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
        settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
        
        shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
        verts = shape.geometry.verts
        faces = shape.geometry.faces
        
        verts_array = np.array(verts).reshape(-1, 3)
        mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts_array, faces=faces)
        
        bounds = mesh.bounds
        z_min, z_max = bounds[0, 2], bounds[1, 2]
        z_mid = (z_min + z_max) / 2
        
        section = mesh.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, z_mid], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
        if section is None:
            return None
            
        path2d = section.to_planar()[0]
        if not path2d.polygons_full:
            return None
            
        return path2d.polygons_full[0]
    except Exception:
        return None

def can_fit_rectangle(polygon: geom.Polygon, width: float, depth: float) -> bool:
    """Check if a rectangle of given dimensions can fit inside the polygon."""
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = polygon.bounds
    poly_width = maxx - minx
    poly_depth = maxy - miny
    
    if poly_width < width or poly_depth < depth:
        if poly_width >= depth and poly_depth >= width:
            pass
        else:
            return False
    
    if not polygon.is_valid:
        polygon = polygon.buffer(0)
        if polygon.is_empty or not polygon.is_valid:

    orientations = [0, 90, 45, 30, 60]
    
    for angle_deg in orientations:
        angle_rad = np.radians(angle_deg)
        cos_a, sin_a = np.cos(angle_rad), np.sin(angle_rad)
        
        centroid = polygon.centroid
        candidate_centers = [centroid]

            for pt in coords:
                point = geom.Point(pt)
                if polygon.contains(point.buffer(1)):
                    candidate_centers.append(point)
        
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = polygon.bounds
        for _ in range(15):

            y = np.random.uniform(miny, maxy)
            pt = geom.Point(x, y)
            if polygon.contains(pt):

                (-width/2, -depth/2),
                (width/2, -depth/2),
                (width/2, depth/2),
                (-width/2, depth/2)
            ]

            for x, y in corners_local:
                xr = x * cos_a - y * sin_a
                yr = x * sin_a + y * cos_a
                corners_rotated.append((cx + xr, cy + yr))
            
            rect = geom.Polygon(corners_rotated)
            if rect.is_valid and polygon.contains(rect):
                return True
    
    return False

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

    # A more human readable name

    # Each style may have diffuse colour RGB codes
    if style.has_diffuse:

        print(style.transparency)

# Indices of material applied per triangle face e.g. [f1m, f2m, ...]
material_ids = shape.geometry.material_ids

    by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Applicable Space Classifications: Balcony, Circulation, Garage, Habitable, 
    Institutional, Lobby, Mercantile, Office, Parking, Production, Refuge,

        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('/path/to/model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violating spaces")

    # Constants for minimum clear space (mm)
    MIN_WIDTH = 760.0  # 30 inches
    MIN_LENGTH = 1220.0  # 48 inches
    
    # Applicable classifications
    APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS = {

        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production',
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }

    if not spaces:

        # Proceed without classification - check all spaces
        classified_spaces = space_data
    
    # Process each space
    settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
    
    for space_info in classified_spaces:
        space = space_info.get('obj')
        classification = space_info.get('classification', 'Unclassified')
        
        if space is None:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        
        # Skip spaces not in applicable classifications
        if classification not in APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS:
            continue
        
        try:
            # Get geometry for the space
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
            faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)
            
            # Create trimesh
            mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts, faces=faces)
            
            # Get z-level for section (mid-height of space)
            min_z, max_z = mesh.bounds[0, 2], mesh.bounds[1, 2]
            mid_z = (min_z + max_z) / 2
            
            # Create horizontal section to get 2D footprint
            section = mesh.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, mid_z], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
            
            if section:

                if path2d.polygons_full:
                    polygon = path2d.polygons_full[0]
                    
                    # Check if the space can fit the minimum rectangle
                    # Use minimum rotated rectangle to find tightest bounding box
                    min_rect = polygon.minimum_rotated_rectangle
                    
                    if isinstance(min_rect, sg.Polygon):

                        coords = list(min_rect.exterior.coords)

                        edge1_len = sg.Point(coords[0]).distance(sg.Point(coords[1]))

                        if max_extent > 1000:  # Likely in millimeters already

                        else:  # Likely in meters
                            scale_factor = 1000.0
                        
                        width_mm = width * scale_factor

                        # Check violation: space is too small in either dimension

        except Exception as e:

#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
grouped_edges = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_edges(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]
grouped_faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape
styles = shape.geometry.materials

for style in styles:
    # Each style is named after the entity class if a default
    # material is applied. Otherwise, it is named "surface-style-{SurfaceStyle.name}"
    # All non-alphanumeric characters are replaced with a "-".
    print(style.original_name())

    # A more human readable name

    # Each style may have diffuse colour RGB codes

    # Each style may have transparency data

This Python code snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an element, and create its OpenCASCADE BRep geometry. It utilizes ifcopenshell.geom.settings to enable Python-OCC and retrieves the transformation and translation part of the shape.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
settings.set("use-python-opencascade", True)

try:
    shape = geom.create_shape(settings, element)
    geometry = shape.geometry # see #1124
    # These are methods of the TopoDS_Shape class from pythonOCC
    shape_gpXYZ = geometry.Location().Transformation().TranslationPart()
    # These are methods of the gpXYZ class from pythonOCC
    print(shape_gpXYZ.X(), shape_gpXYZ.Y(), shape_gpXYZ.Z())
except:
    print("Shape creation failed")
```

from scipy.spatial import ConvexHull

# Test the function development on multiple models

    '/home/sffc348/Repos/cobbie/acc/bim_models/ac20/arc.ifc',

    '/home/sffc348/Repos/cobbie/acc/bim_models/duplex/arc.ifc'
]

def check_space_fits(space, model, req_width_m=0.76, req_depth_m=1.22):
    """Check if a space can fit the required clear floor area."""
    settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    try:
        shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
        verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
        
        if len(verts) == 0:
            return False
        
        # Get unique XY points (footprint)
        xy_points = verts[:, :2]
        xy_points_rounded = np.round(xy_points, decimals=6)
        unique_points = np.unique(xy_points_rounded, axis=0)
        
        if len(unique_points) < 3:
            return False
        
        # Create convex hull
        try:
            hull = ConvexHull(unique_points)
            hull_points = unique_points[hull.vertices]
            
            # Get minimum rotated rectangle
            multi_point = MultiPoint([tuple(p) for p in hull_points])
            min_rect = multi_point.minimum_rotated_rectangle
            
            # Get bounds of rotated rectangle
            minx, miny, maxx, maxy = min_rect.bounds
            rect_dim_x = maxx - minx
            rect_dim_y = maxy - miny
            
            # Check if required rectangle fits (in either orientation)
            fits = (rect_dim_x >= req_width_m and rect_dim_y >= req_depth_m) or \
                   (rect_dim_x >= req_depth_m and rect_dim_y >= req_width_m)
            
            return not fits  # Returns True if VIOLATION (doesn't fit)
            
        except Exception:
            # Fallback to bounding box if convex hull fails
            minx, miny = unique_points.min(axis=0)
            maxx, maxy = unique_points.max(axis=0)
            dim_x = maxx - minx
            dim_y = maxy - miny
            
            fits = (dim_x >= req_width_m and dim_y >= req_depth_m) or \
                   (dim_x >= req_depth_m and dim_y >= req_width_m)
            
            return not fits
            
    except Exception:
        return False

def get_space_footprint(space, model) -> Optional[geom.Polygon]:
    """Extract 2D footprint from an IfcSpace."""
    try:
        settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
        settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
        
        shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
        verts = shape.geometry.verts
        faces = shape.geometry.faces
        
        verts_array = np.array(verts).reshape(-1, 3)
        mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts_array, faces=faces)
        
        bounds = mesh.bounds
        z_min, z_max = bounds[0, 2], bounds[1, 2]
        z_mid = (z_min + z_max) / 2
        
        section = mesh.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, z_mid], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
        if section is None:
            return None
            
        path2d = section.to_planar()[0]
        if not path2d.polygons_full:
            return None
            
        return path2d.polygons_full[0]
    except Exception:
        return None

def can_fit_rectangle(polygon: geom.Polygon, width: float, depth: float) -> bool:
    """Check if a rectangle of given dimensions can fit inside the polygon."""
    minx, miny, maxx, maxy = polygon.bounds
    poly_width = maxx - minx
    poly_depth = maxy - miny
    
    if poly_width < width or poly_depth < depth:
        if poly_width >= depth and poly_depth >= width:
            pass
        else:
            return False
    
    if not polygon.is_valid:
        polygon = polygon.buffer(0)
        if polygon.is_empty or not polygon.is_valid:
            return False
    
    orientations = [0, 90, 45, 30, 60]
    
    for angle_deg in orientations:
        angle_rad = np.radians(angle_deg)
        cos_a, sin_a = np.cos(angle_rad), np.sin(angle_rad)
        
        centroid = polygon.centroid
        candidate_centers = [centroid]
        
        if isinstance(polygon, geom.Polygon):
            coords = list(polygon.exterior.coords)
            for pt in coords:
                point = geom.Point(pt)
                if polygon.contains(point.buffer(1)):
                    candidate_centers.append(point)
        
        minx, miny, maxx, maxy = polygon.bounds
        for _ in range(15):
            x = np.random.uniform(minx, maxx)
            y = np.random.uniform(miny, maxy)
            pt = geom.Point(x, y)
            if polygon.contains(pt):
                candidate_centers.append(pt)
        
        for center in candidate_centers:
            cx, cy = center.x, center.y
            corners_local = [
                (-width/2, -depth/2),
                (width/2, -depth/2),
                (width/2, depth/2),
                (-width/2, depth/2)
            ]
            
            corners_rotated = []
            for x, y in corners_local:
                xr = x * cos_a - y * sin_a
                yr = x * sin_a + y * cos_a
                corners_rotated.append((cx + xr, cy + yr))
            
            rect = geom.Polygon(corners_rotated)
            if rect.is_valid and polygon.contains(rect):
                return True
    
    return False

def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Check if spaces have accessible clear floor space per rule 305.3.
    
    Rule: 305.3 Size
    The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) minimum

    Args:

    """
    model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')

    space_dicts = [{'guid': s.GlobalId, 'name': s.LongName or s.Name or ''} for s in spaces]
    classified_spaces = classify_spaces(space_dicts, path_ifc_model)
    
    applicable_classifications = {

        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    violating_guids = []
    min_width = 760  # mm
    min_depth = 1220  # mm
    
    for i, space in enumerate(spaces):

import ifcopenshell

import numpy as np
from typing import List, Optional
import warnings

def get_space_footprint(space, model) -> Optional[geom.Polygon]:
    """Extract 2D footprint from an IfcSpace."""
    try:
        settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
        settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
        
        shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
        verts = shape.geometry.verts
        faces = shape.geometry.faces
        
        verts_array = np.array(verts).reshape(-1, 3)
        mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts_array, faces=faces)
        
        bounds = mesh.bounds
        z_min, z_max = bounds[0, 2], bounds[1, 2]
        z_mid = (z_min + z_max) / 2
        
        section = mesh.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, z_mid], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
        if section is None:
            return None
            
        path2d = section.to_planar()[0]
        if not path2d.polygons_full:
            return None
            
        return path2d.polygons_full[0]

        return None

### Create IFC Beam with Geometry Representation

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/geometry_creation.rst

This snippet shows how to create an IfcBeam entity, define its placement, assign it a type, and create a geometric representation using a predefined profile. It utilizes IFCopenShell's API for entity creation and geometry handling.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.api
import ifcopenshell.util.representation
from ifcopenshell import geom

# Assume 'model', 'beam_type', and 'hea100' are pre-defined IFC objects/values
# Example: model = ifcopenshell.file.create()
# Example: beam_type = ifcopenshell.api.type.add_type(model, 'B1BeamType', 'IfcBeam')
# Example: hea100 = ifcopenshell.api.material.add_profile(model, 'HEA100', 'IPE')

# Create an IfcBeam entity
beam = ifcopenshell.api.root.create_entity(model, ifc_class="IfcBeam")

# Edit the object placement for the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.edit_object_placement(model, product=beam)

# Assign the beam type to the created beam
ifcopenshell.api.type.assign_type(model, related_objects=[beam], relating_type=beam_type)

# Get the 'Body' model context
body = ifcopenshell.util.representation.get_context(model, "Model", "Body", "MODEL_VIEW")

# Create a profile representation for the beam's geometry
representation = geom.add_profile_representation(model, context=body, profile=hea100, depth=1)

# Assign the created geometry representation back to the beam
ifcopenshell.api.geometry.assign_representation(model, product=beam, representation=representation)
```

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]

# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]

# A list of styles that are relevant to this shape

def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Check ADA 305.3 Size compliance for spaces in an IFC model.
    
    Rule 305.3: The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) minimum 
    by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Applicable Space Classifications: Balcony, Circulation, Garage, Habitable, 
    Institutional, Lobby, Mercantile, Office, Parking, Production, Refuge, 
    Stair Hall, Workplace
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List[str]: List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate the rule (have 
                   inaccessible areas where a 760mm x 1220mm clear space cannot fit).
                   Returns empty list if no violations or if model cannot be processed.
                   
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('/path/to/model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violating spaces")
    """
    # Constants for minimum clear space (mm)
    MIN_WIDTH = 760.0  # 30 inches
    MIN_LENGTH = 1220.0  # 48 inches
    
    # Applicable classifications
    APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional',
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production',
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped = 0
    
    try:
        model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Could not open IFC model: {e}")
        return []
    
    # Get all spaces
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Prepare space data for classification
    space_data = []
    for space in spaces:
        space_info = {
            'guid': space.GlobalId,
            'name': space.LongName or space.Name or "",
            'obj': space
        }
        space_data.append(space_info)
    
    # Classify spaces
    try:
        classified_spaces = classify_spaces(space_data, path_ifc_model)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Could not classify spaces: {e}")
        # Proceed without classification - check all spaces
        classified_spaces = space_data
    
    # Process each space
    settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
    
    for space_info in classified_spaces:
        space = space_info.get('obj')
        classification = space_info.get('classification', 'Unclassified')
        
        if space is None:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        
        # Skip spaces not in applicable classifications
        if classification not in APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS:
            continue
        
        try:
            # Get geometry for the space
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
            faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)
            
            # Create trimesh
            mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts, faces=faces)
            
            # Get z-level for section (mid-height of space)
            min_z, max_z = mesh.bounds[0, 2], mesh.bounds[1, 2]
            mid_z = (min_z + max_z) / 2
            
            # Create horizontal section to get 2D footprint
            section = mesh.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, mid_z], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
            
            if section:
                path2d = section.to_planar()[0]
                if path2d.polygons_full:
                    polygon = path2d.polygons_full[0]
                    
                    # Check if the space can fit the minimum rectangle
                    # Use minimum rotated rectangle to find tightest bounding box
                    min_rect = polygon.minimum_rotated_rectangle
                    
                    if isinstance(min_rect, sg.Polygon):
                        # Get the dimensions of the minimum rotated rectangle
                        coords = list(min_rect.exterior.coords)
                        # Calculate edge lengths
                        edge1_len = sg.Point(coords[0]).distance(sg.Point(coords[1]))
                        edge2_len = sg.Point(coords[1]).distance(sg.Point(coords[2]))
                        
                        # The rectangle dimensions are the two perpendicular edge lengths
                        width = min(edge1_len, edge2_len)
                        length = max(edge1_len, edge2_len)
                        
                        # Convert to mm (IFC models are typically in mm, but check bounds)
                        # If bounds suggest meters (large numbers), convert
                        max_extent = max(mesh.extents)
                        if max_extent > 1000:  # Likely in millimeters already
                            scale_factor = 1.0
                        else:  # Likely in meters
                            scale_factor = 1000.0
                        
                        width_mm = width * scale_factor
                        length_mm = length * scale_factor
                        
                        # Check violation: space is too small in either dimension
                        if width_mm < MIN_WIDTH or length_mm < MIN_LENGTH:
                            violating_guids.append(space.GlobalId)
            else:
                # No section could be created - space may have degenerate geometry
                # Consider this a violation as it indicates inaccessible area
                violating_guids.append(space.GlobalId)
                
        except Exception as e:
            # If geometry processing fails, consider it a potential violation
            # (inaccessible area due to geometry issues)
            skipped += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped} spaces due to geometry processing errors")

# Define the helper function
def check_305_3_size(path_ifc_model: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Check ADA 305.3 Size compliance for spaces in an IFC model.
    
    Rule 305.3: The clear floor or ground space shall be 30 inches (760 mm) minimum 
    by 48 inches (1220 mm) minimum.
    
    Applicable Space Classifications: Balcony, Circulation, Garage, Habitable, 
    Institutional, Lobby, Mercantile, Office, Parking, Production, Refuge, 
    Stair Hall, Workplace
    
    Args:
        path_ifc_model: Path to the IFC model file.
        
    Returns:
        List[str]: List of IFC GUIDs of spaces that violate the rule (have 
                   inaccessible areas where a 760mm x 1220mm clear space cannot fit).
                   Returns empty list if no violations or if model cannot be processed.
                   
    Example:
        >>> violations = check_305_3_size('/path/to/model.ifc')
        >>> print(f"Found {len(violations)} violating spaces")
    """
    # Constants for minimum clear space (mm)
    MIN_WIDTH = 760.0  # 30 inches
    MIN_LENGTH = 1220.0  # 48 inches
    
    # Applicable classifications
    APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS = {
        'Balcony', 'Circulation', 'Garage', 'Habitable', 'Institutional',
        'Lobby', 'Mercantile', 'Office', 'Parking', 'Production',
        'Refuge', 'Stair Hall', 'Workplace'
    }
    
    violating_guids = []
    skipped = 0
    
    try:
        model = ifcopenshell.open(path_ifc_model)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Could not open IFC model: {e}")
        return []
    
    # Get all spaces
    spaces = model.by_type('IfcSpace')
    if not spaces:
        return []
    
    # Prepare space data for classification
    space_data = []
    for space in spaces:
        space_info = {
            'guid': space.GlobalId,
            'name': space.LongName or space.Name or "",
            'obj': space
        }
        space_data.append(space_info)
    
    # Classify spaces
    try:
        classified_spaces = classify_spaces(space_data, path_ifc_model)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Warning: Could not classify spaces: {e}")
        # Proceed without classification - check all spaces
        classified_spaces = space_data
    
    # Process each space
    settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    settings.set(settings.USE_WORLD_COORDS, True)
    
    for space_info in classified_spaces:
        space = space_info.get('obj')
        classification = space_info.get('classification', 'Unclassified')
        
        if space is None:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        
        # Skip spaces not in applicable classifications
        if classification not in APPLICABLE_CLASSIFICATIONS:
            continue
        
        try:
            # Get geometry for the space
            shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, space)
            verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
            faces = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_faces(shape.geometry)
            
            # Create trimesh
            mesh = trimesh.Trimesh(vertices=verts, faces=faces)
            
            # Get z-level for section (mid-height of space)
            min_z, max_z = mesh.bounds[0, 2], mesh.bounds[1, 2]
            mid_z = (min_z + max_z) / 2
            
            # Create horizontal section to get 2D footprint
            section = mesh.section(plane_origin=[0, 0, mid_z], plane_normal=[0, 0, 1])
            
            if section:
                path2d = section.to_planar()[0]
                if path2d.polygons_full:
                    polygon = path2d.polygons_full[0]
                    
                    # Check if the space can fit the minimum rectangle
                    # Use minimum rotated rectangle to find tightest bounding box
                    min_rect = polygon.minimum_rotated_rectangle
                    
                    if isinstance(min_rect, sg.Polygon):
                        # Get the dimensions of the minimum rotated rectangle
                        coords = list(min_rect.exterior.coords)
                        # Calculate edge lengths
                        edge1_len = sg.Point(coords[0]).distance(sg.Point(coords[1]))
                        edge2_len = sg.Point(coords[1]).distance(sg.Point(coords[2]))
                        
                        # The rectangle dimensions are the two perpendicular edge lengths
                        width = min(edge1_len, edge2_len)
                        length = max(edge1_len, edge2_len)
                        
                        # Check violation: space is too small in either dimension
                        # Assuming IFC units are millimeters (typical)
                        if width < MIN_WIDTH or length < MIN_LENGTH:
                            violating_guids.append(space.GlobalId)
            else:
                # No section could be created - space may have degenerate geometry
                # Consider this a violation as it indicates inaccessible area
                violating_guids.append(space.GlobalId)
                
        except Exception as e:
            # If geometry processing fails, consider it a potential violation
            # (inaccessible area due to geometry issues)
            skipped += 1
            continue
    
    if skipped > 0:
        print(f"Warning: Skipped {skipped} spaces due to geometry processing errors")
    
    return violating_guids

This Python snippet demonstrates how to open an IFC file, select an IfcWall element, and process it into a shape using ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(). It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. This is useful for understanding individual geometry processing but not recommended for practical applications due to performance limitations.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# X Y Z of vertices in flattened list e.g. [v1x, v1y, v1z, v2x, v2y, v2z, ...]
# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# Indices of vertices per edge e.g. [e1v1, e1v2, e2v1, e2v2, ...]
# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.
edges = shape.geometry.edges

# Indices of vertices per triangle face e.g. [f1v1, f1v2, f1v3, f2v1, f2v2, f2v3, ...]
# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# Since the lists are flattened, you may prefer to group them like so depending on your geometry kernel
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]

# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]

# A nested numpy array e.g. [[f1v1, f1v2, f1v3], [f2v1, f2v2, f2v3], ...]

import ifcopenshell

    geometry = shape.geometry # see #1124
    # These are methods of the TopoDS_Shape class from pythonOCC

    print("Shape creation failed")

### Get XYZ Coordinates of an IFC Element with IfcOpenShell

Source: https://github.com/ifcopenshell/ifcopenshell/blob/v0.8.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/docs/ifcopenshell-python/code_examples.rst

This example shows how to extract the XYZ coordinates (location) of an IFC element from its placement information. It uses `ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement` to obtain the transformation matrix and then extracts the translation vector. Assumes an IFC model is loaded and an 'IfcWall' instance is available.

```python
import ifcopenshell
import ifcopenshell.util.placement

model = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')

wall = model.by_type("IfcWall")[0]
# This returns a 4x4 matrix, including the location and rotation. For example:
# array([[ 1.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00, 2.00000000e+00],
#        [ 0.00000000e+00,  1.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00, 3.00000000e+00],

#        [ 0.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00,  0.00000000e+00, 1.00000000e+00]])
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.placement.get_local_placement(wall.ObjectPlacement)
# The last column holds the XYZ values, such as:
# array([ 2.00000000e+00,  3.00000000e+00,  5.00000000e+00])
print(matrix[:,3][:3])

It shows how to extract the element's GUID, ID, geometry ID, transformation matrix, vertices, edges, faces, and material information. import ifcopenshell.geom
import ifcopenshell.util.shape

ifc_file = ifcopenshell.open('model.ifc')
element = ifc_file.by_type('IfcWall')[0]

settings = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
shape = ifcopenshell.geom.create_shape(settings, element)

# The GUID of the element we processed
print(shape.guid)

# The ID of the element we processed
print(shape.id)

# The element we are processing
print(ifc_file.by_guid(shape.guid))

# A unique geometry ID, useful to check whether or not two geometries are
# identical for caching and reuse. The naming scheme is:
# IfcShapeRepresentation.id{-layerset-LayerSet.id}{-material-Material.id}{-openings-[Opening n.id ...]}{-world-coords}
print(shape.geometry.id)

# A 4x4 matrix representing the location and rotation of the element, in the form:
# [ [ x_x, y_x, z_x, x   ]
#   [ x_y, y_y, z_y, y   ]
#   [ x_z, y_z, z_z, z   ]
#   [ 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] ]
# The position is given by the last column: (x, y, z)
# The rotation is described by the first three columns, by explicitly specifying the local X, Y, Z axes.
# The first column is a normalised vector of the local X axis: (x_x, x_y, x_z)
# The second column is a normalised vector of the local Y axis: (y_x, y_y, y_z)
# The third column is a normalised vector of the local Z axis: (z_x, z_y, z_z)
# The axes follow a right-handed coordinate system.
# Objects are never scaled, so the scale factor of the matrix is always 1.
matrix = shape.transformation.matrix

# For convenience, you might want the matrix as a nested numpy array, so you can do matrix math.
matrix = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_shape_matrix(shape)

# You can also extract the XYZ location of the matrix.
location = matrix[:,3][0:3]

# These vertices are local relative to the shape's transformation matrix.
verts = shape.geometry.verts

# If the geometry is mesh-like, edges contain the original edges.
# These may be quads or ngons and not necessarily triangles.

# Note that faces are always triangles.
faces = shape.geometry.faces

# A nested numpy array e.g. [[v1x, v1y, v1z], [v2x, v2y, v2z], ...]
grouped_verts = ifcopenshell.util.shape.get_vertices(shape.geometry)
# A nested numpy array e.g. [[e1v1, e1v2], [e2v1, e2v2], ...]
